task_3.title: Preserve full visible scope for derived block rendering
task_3.description: The 2.9.3 update fixes Jinja block rendering so derived contexts use the full currently visible template scope. This prevents scoped blocks and other block evaluations in independent same-template contexts from losing locally overridden values.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that block rendering in Jinja uses the full currently visible template scope when a derived context is created, so scoped blocks and similar block evaluations do not lose variables that were overridden in a local scope.

expectation.grounded: When Jinja creates a derived rendering context within the same template, that context should reflect the complete visible variable set available through the current context, not only explicitly stored local variables. As a result, `{% block ... scoped %}` and other block evaluations that run through a derived context should observe variables overridden by enclosing local scopes and retain access to inherited values already visible at the render site.
expectation.conceptual: Blocks that render in nested or independent template contexts should behave as if they were executed with the same visible data the template had at that point. If a value was overridden in a nearer scope, the block should use that value instead of acting as though the override never happened.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress same-template derived-context behavior: block rendering should continue to use the current evaluation state and block definitions while exposing the full resolved scope visible at the point of rendering. The fix must preserve access to both inherited values and local overrides without narrowing visibility compared with the active context.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should broaden block visibility to match the caller's actual scope without changing unrelated rendering semantics. Existing block execution should keep working, but variables that are already visible where the block is entered must remain visible inside it.

behavior: A derived rendering context now carries the full merged visible template scope for block evaluation.
If a variable is overridden in a local scope before entering a scoped block, the block renders with the overridden value.
Block evaluations that occur through independent same-template contexts no longer lose access to variables that were visible at the point where rendering entered the block.
acceptance_criteria: When a template overrides a variable inside a local scope and then renders a `scoped` block within that scope, the block should output the locally overridden value.

When Jinja renders a block through a derived context in the same template, the block should have access to the same visible variables that were available at the point where the derived context was created.
When block rendering is reached through another same-template construct that uses a derived context, it should render using the active visible scope rather than dropping locally visible values.

task_2.title: Fix inconsistent inner-scope variable reads
task_2.description: Jinja 2.9.3 corrects a scoping regression introduced in 2.9.x so that nested template scopes read an existing outer variable consistently even when that same name is assigned locally later in the inner scope. The change preserves scope isolation, so local assignments still do not write back to the outer scope.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when a template reads a variable inside an inner scope and later assigns to that same variable name within the inner scope, the pre-assignment read consistently uses the nearest outer value when one exists, instead of behaving as undefined. Ensure that this fix does not restore legacy behavior where inner-scope assignments could mutate or leak into the outer scope.

expectation.grounded: During template rendering, constructs that create an inner scope, including loop bodies and scoped assignments, must treat a name that is read before a local assignment as an alias to the nearest outer binding if one exists. If no outer binding exists, the name should continue to behave as undefined until the local assignment occurs. After the local assignment, subsequent reads in that inner scope should observe the local value, and the outer binding must remain unchanged after the inner scope finishes.
expectation.conceptual: Nested template scopes should consistently inherit an existing variable value for reads that happen before a same-named local assignment, while still keeping the assignment local to that nested scope. If no outer value exists, the read should stay undefined until the variable is assigned locally.

constraints.grounded: Do not reintroduce pre-2.9 behavior where assigning to a name inside a loop or other inner scope can partially update the outer scope or carry that assignment across scope boundaries. Preserve undefined behavior for names with no outer binding before local assignment.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must improve read consistency without changing scope isolation rules. Local assignments inside nested scopes must remain local, and missing outer values must not be replaced with invented defaults.

behavior: A read of a variable in an inner scope before a later local assignment now resolves to the nearest outer value when that value exists.
If the same variable name has no outer binding, reading it before local assignment continues to behave as undefined.
Once the variable is assigned inside the inner scope, later reads in that scope use the newly assigned local value.
Leaving the inner scope does not modify the outer variable, and the upgrade does not restore older behavior that allowed limited assignment back to outer scopes.
acceptance_criteria: When a template enters a nested scope, reads variable `x`, and later assigns `x` inside that scope, it should render the outer `x` value for the pre-assignment read if an outer `x` exists.
When no outer `x` exists, reading `x` before its local assignment in a nested scope should still behave as undefined.
When `x` is assigned inside the nested scope, subsequent reads of `x` in that same scope should reflect the new local value.
When rendering continues after the nested scope ends, the outer `x` should remain unchanged by the inner assignment.

task_1.title: Restore block rendering inside macros
task_1.description: Upgrading to 2.9.3 restores correct output for template blocks rendered from buffered template contexts, especially macros. In 2.9.2 on Python 3, these blocks could surface an internal generator representation instead of the intended rendered content; 2.9.3 returns normal block output again while preserving block scoping behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that templates render block content correctly when blocks are used inside macros or similar buffered rendering contexts, so Python 3 output shows the intended rendered text rather than an internal generator representation.

expectation.grounded: In Jinja2 2.9.3, rendering a macro that contains a `{% block %}` must produce the block's rendered content on Python 3 instead of exposing a generator object representation. Block rendering through this path must continue to respect scoped block semantics, so a `scoped` block resolves values from the active rendering context.
expectation.conceptual: Templates that combine macros and blocks should render the same human-readable output that the block defines. If block scope affects which values are visible, the rendered result should still reflect the correct in-scope data.

constraints.grounded: The fix must correct block rendering only for the affected runtime path and must not change observable behavior for normal block rendering outside buffered contexts, alter async template behavior, or weaken existing scoped-context resolution for blocks.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should remove the broken output without changing unrelated template behavior. Existing rendering modes and context rules should continue to behave as before except for the corrected block output.

behavior: A block rendered from within a macro on Python 3 now contributes its evaluated text to the final template output instead of showing an internal generator representation.
Blocks rendered in buffered template execution paths behave like normal rendered content rather than leaking internal iteration details into user-visible output.
Scoped blocks rendered through the corrected path continue to use the currently active scoped values when producing output.
acceptance_criteria: When a template defines a macro containing a block and the macro is rendered on Python 3, it should output the block's rendered text rather than an object-style generator representation.
When block output is produced through a buffered rendering path, the final rendered template should contain the block content as ordinary text.
When a scoped block is rendered while a local scope overrides a value, the rendered block output should reflect the overridden in-scope value.

task_4.title: Correct `with` block scoping semantics
task_4.description: Version 2.9.3 changes `with` block handling so header expressions are evaluated using the surrounding context before block-local names are introduced, fixing edge-case scoping bugs. It also adds an internal `With` node so extensions can generate the same behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `with` statements follow the updated scoping model so values declared in a `with` header are computed from the enclosing context, then exposed only as temporary names inside the block, avoiding edge-case misresolution between sibling assignments.

expectation.grounded: The `with` statement should parse and compile as a dedicated `With` node. For `with` declarations such as multiple `target=value` pairs, each value expression must be evaluated in the enclosing frame before the corresponding targets are bound in the inner block scope. The `with` body should then execute with those bound local names, and extensions should be able to emit the internal `With` node to obtain the same semantics.
expectation.conceptual: A `with` block should behave like creating a temporary local scope from a snapshot of expressions in the current context. Names introduced by the block should be visible inside the block, but earlier names in the same `with` declaration must not influence how later declarations are computed.

constraints.grounded: Preserve the existing isolation of `with` blocks: declared names remain local to the block body, multi-assignment `with` syntax continues to work, and the body still receives all declared bindings. The change should only affect how header expressions are resolved and should apply equally to parser-generated and extension-generated `With` nodes.
constraints.conceptual: Keep `with` blocks temporary and predictable. The update should correct expression scoping at block entry without changing normal visibility inside the block or leaking temporary names after the block ends.

behavior: `with` statements use a dedicated internal `With` node instead of being modeled as a generic scope containing assignment statements.
Each expression in a `with` header is resolved against the surrounding context rather than against names introduced earlier in the same header.
After those expressions are evaluated, the resulting values are bound to block-local targets and made available while rendering the `with` body.
Values introduced by a `with` block remain confined to that block and do not replace the outer context after the block ends.
Extensions can generate `With` nodes directly and receive the same runtime behavior as the built-in `with` statement.
acceptance_criteria: When a `with` block declares multiple names and a later initializer references a name that is also assigned earlier in the same header, it should resolve that reference from the enclosing context, not from the earlier block-local assignment.
When rendering inside a `with` block, the block body should see the local names bound from the header expressions.
When rendering continues after `endwith`, outer variables should retain their original values and should not be overwritten by temporary `with` bindings.
When an extension emits an internal `With` node equivalent to a parsed `with` statement, it should produce the same scoping and rendering behavior.
